source.title: Towards efficient and effective unlearning of large language models for recommendation
source.authors: Hangyu Wang; Jianghao Lin; Bo Chen; Yang Yang; Rui-Ming Tang; Wei-Nan Zhang; Yong Yu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including conclusion and references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses unlearning methods for recommendation-data deletion and reports how they perform there. It does not test whether unlearned knowledge can be recovered by the attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments measure recommendation performance and output-distribution distance from a retrained model on forgotten recommendation data. They do not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. The rows below record baseline unlearning results in this related recommendation setting; they do not measure any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes E2URec for recommendation-data unlearning in T5 and BART recommenders. It reports only utility (AUC/ACC/LogLoss), output distance from a retrained model (JSD, L2) and efficiency. There is no relearning, activation-ablation, quantization or prompting attack. There is no near-chance accuracy test on targeted knowledge, and no robustness claim against recovery. Its results therefore bear on no version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude E2URec forgets specific recommendation data efficiently via LoRA, without harming recommendation performance, and outperforms baselines on two datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The proposed approach uses LoRA and forgetting/remembering teachers for deleting recommendation interaction data; the paper does not use or test the claim's recovery-attack procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported settings vary dataset and backbone (T5-base, T5-large, and BART-base).

fits_no_version.finding: On forgotten interaction data, LoRA teacher-student unlearning (E2URec) gives the smallest JSD/L2 to a retrained recommender (e.g., ML-1M JSD 1.91 vs 3.67–4.64). Gradient-negation baselines are further from retrain. Recommendation AUC is kept near the original.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLM recommenders, distillation-style unlearning approximates retrained-model outputs on forgotten data more closely than gradient-ascent baselines while preserving utility.

record.problems: The results concern recommendation interaction data rather than the targeted knowledge and recovery attacks in the claim. The reported uncertainty fields are absent, and the unlearning metrics measure distance from retrained-model outputs rather than attack-based recoverability.
record.rows_left_out: The tables also report AUC, ACC, LogLoss, time, and parameter counts, but those recommendation utility and efficiency measures do not bear on the claim versions. Results for SISA and RecEraser are omitted because they are recommendation-unlearning comparators rather than the LLM-unlearning baselines recorded here. E2URec's own comparative results are not included as rows under the rule excluding a study's new method compared with other methods.

untested.parts: No accuracy-near-chance measure on targeted knowledge and no recovery attacks. Forgetting is measured only as JSD/L2 distance to a retrained recommender.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deleting.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
E2URec is a new unlearning method, but the paper makes no claim about resisting recovery attacks and tests none.

record.verdict_notes: The setting is recommendation unlearning, with forgetting judged by output similarity to a retrained model. Nothing in the paper probes whether forgotten information is recoverable, so it neither supports nor challenges shallow unlearning. The paper cites Eldan & Russinovich (an original source) only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance, recovery by simple attacks, or the specified general-ability criterion.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning attack or relearning set is evaluated.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking access versus deleting knowledge is evaluated.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery attack is evaluated.
The paper proposes a recommendation-unlearning method but does not test its resistance to the attacks listed in the claim.

rows.subject: T5-base
rows.operation_detail: NegKL recommendation unlearning; KL loss is negated on forgotten data
rows.measure: JSD on forgotten data versus retrained model
rows.baseline: Retrained model is the stated comparison target; numeric baseline not stated
rows.note: The paper defines smaller JSD as better unlearning; this is a recommendation-data result, not a recovery-attack result.
rows.check: Applies to all rows r01–r24. They are baseline values (NegKL, NegGrad, Bad-T) in a comparison with the study's own method (E2URec), so they arguably should not be rows. Values are in % per the table captions. For r01–r12, the T5-base size can be read from #Params (about 2.2e8), not 'not stated'.
